assumptions: Water stand-in (Steam Tables IAPWS-IF97) with evaporator feed_x_NaCl salt balance and Sparrow BPE per run_process evaporator description; electrolyte phase equilibria omitted, so stream T is water saturation and brine boiling temperature is the unit brine_T_C.

Data-sheet Modelling scope governs over full P&ID topology for the as-built question: feed preheat train (BCC-1, BP-1, CST-1, BPF-1) is not solved; VRE feed is taken as boundary feeds S11 = 264.9 t/h at 125.6 C plus S7 = 98.0 t/h elutriating brine at 60 C, both from data sheet Table I rows. Condensate-to-brine recovery connections 9, 21, 22, 24 and brine connections 2, 19 are therefore boundary flows, not closed loops.

Closed CH1 steam loop is unfolded once-through per instructions: utility feed S36 = 251.7 t/h at 135 C, 3.08 bar(a) (data sheet row, stream 36) drives VRE-1 heating and leaves as S21_COND condensate; it is not recycled. The compressor discharge return is solved separately through mixer MX-DESH to terminal stream S36_RETURN as a desuperheating check.

Turbine exhaust S33 is a fixed utility feed (utility:true, does not scale): 15.9 t/h at 3.08 bar(a) from data sheet row; its temperature is not stated in the data sheet and is assumed 135 C (equal to the desuperheated steam temperature) - stated assumption, not a measured value.

Desuperheater is not drawn on FIG. 1 (data sheet note) and is modelled as mixer MX-DESH; spray SPRAY = 14.0 t/h condensate at 134.4 C (CH1 condensate temperature, data sheet row stream 21) calibrated in run as-built-base so the mixer outlet S36_RETURN is saturated at 134.43 C. Spray rate itself is not a Table I measured value.

CH1 is included in VRE-1 and CH2 in PE-1 (P&ID equipment notes: VRE-1 'includes CH1', PE-1 'includes CH2'); there are no separate CH1/CH2 P&ID tags, so heater area/U limits are placed on VRE-1/PE-1. Ratings are the data-sheet ILLUSTRATIVE ratings used exactly as given, never raised: CH1 8,800 m2 U 2,000 W/m2K in service, CH2 1,500 m2 U 1,500 W/m2K.

VRC-1 efficiency 75% is an assumed value only to estimate shaft duty (patent states shaft power not stated, data sheet Equipment ratings); discharge pressure 3.08 bar(a) and suction capacity 226.8 t/h are data-sheet values. Compressor discharge temperature is therefore not a calibrated measurement.

Splitter fractions are calibration parameters, not equipment ratings: VRE liquid purge fraction 0.378 calibrated to Table I purge 47.6 t/h; VRE vapour excess fraction 0.0843 = Table I ratio 20.9/(226.8+20.9); PE liquid disposal fraction 0.247 calibrated to Table I disposal 6.8 t/h.
Salt product streams S13_SALT and S20_SALT are water-stand-in liquid (crystals plus mother liquor); the dry salt rate is the sum of the evaporator salt_kg_h outputs, not the stream kg/h.

Cogeneration and downstream items CGT-1, HRSG-1, ST-1, GEN-1, SRP-1, DWF-1, CST-1 carry no process ratings in the P&ID (all capacity_kW/flow_gpm null) or data sheet and are represented only by their boundary streams (S33 turbine exhaust in; S13/S20 salt out; S15 disposal out); GEN-1 is electrical only.

Forced-circulation pump is not drawn in FIG. 1 and its 15,000 m3/h rating is ILLUSTRATIVE with no Table I circulation flow, head or temperature-rise measurement; the CH1 brine rise <=3 K rule therefore cannot be checked in this spec and is not represented as a limit - no rating was invented for it.

P&ID data_quality/read_notes state no capacities, flows or valve types are printed and connections use reference numerals 1-37; all values therefore come from the data sheet Table I/ratings, and P&ID printed evaporator conditions (10 PSIG 258F = 1.70 bar(a)/125.6 C; 0 PSIG 228F = 1.01 bar(a)/108.9 C) agree with the data sheet - no P&ID-vs-datasheet conflict was found. Patent Table I is not exactly heat-closed: with Table I heating steam the simulator boil-up is heat-limited below Table I vapour/salt rates; deviations are reported in calibration, not hidden by raising any rating.

energy.note: An overall energy balance is not closed: the simulator's streams do not report enthalpy. Each evaporator's heat balance is checked instead (within 2 %; a model is blocked above 10 %).
